variants.name: Current architecture
variants.summary: System level: the processes that run, and what they keep. Drill into each application for its internal modules.

nodes.name: Agent CLI
nodes.responsibility: Authors named boards: one short-lived process per command, writing no board itself
nodes.description: Every board operation reaches the Archboard server over HTTP. Two commands draw for themselves: rasterize takes the SVG the server made into a headless browser here, and record opens the server's own page in one and writes the narrated walkthrough to a video file, through ffmpeg when one is at hand. repo add writes this machine's list of checkouts itself.

nodes.name: Archboard server
nodes.responsibility: Owns every board, draws every view, and answers both applications
nodes.description: One process. Board persistence, the renderer, the pane sockets and the agent workbench all live in it; the Codex app-server is its private child.

nodes.name: Browser
nodes.responsibility: Reads architecture; owns the camera, the view, the walkthrough and the selection, and nothing else
nodes.description: It also carries voice: the Archboard server negotiates the session with Codex for the page, and the microphone and the voice then travel over the connection that negotiation opens.

nodes.name: Board vault
nodes.responsibility: One document per board, holding every variant of it
nodes.description: Tracked in the repository. The file is the board and nothing holds a copy of it: an accepted write is on disk, fsync included, before it is answered (ADR 0015, ADR 0023).

nodes.name: Codex app-server
nodes.responsibility: Runs the linked agent threads, as one private child of the Archboard server
nodes.description: Its own process group, spoken to over stdio; what it keeps is in the Codex home. Its threads author boards the way any agent does, by running the CLI from a sandbox that reaches the server over localhost. Archboard's side of it is the agent workbench inside the Archboard server.

nodes.name: Repository checkout
nodes.responsibility: The source a node's binding resolves to on this machine
nodes.description: A binding names a repository identity and a path inside it, which are the same in every clone; a machine-local registry is the only place a directory on one machine is written down.

nodes.name: Skill evaluation
nodes.responsibility: Measures one version of the agent skill against another, on real authors and real checkouts
nodes.description: Started by a person, never by the gate: every author run and the grading session call a model.

nodes.name: Headless Chromium
nodes.responsibility: Paints an SVG and answers with the bitmap, or opens the Archboard server's page and captures a narrated walkthrough, when a command asks

nodes.name: Codex home
nodes.responsibility: Codex's sign-in, config and threads, shared by every Archboard server on this machine
nodes.description: An archboard-only CODEX_HOME under the state directory, readable by nobody else. One sign-in serves every server, since Codex takes several processes on one home; what a server keeps about its own child, the owner lock and the epoch ledger, sits under its port. The server fills in the config it needs (auto-review approvals, a sandbox with network access) and keeps what Codex or the user set.

edges.label: photograph a board, record a walkthrough
one per run, on its own port

beats.heading: Agents author, people read
beats.body: An agent states meaning through the CLI. The Archboard server checks the write, takes the board's lease, commits the whole family to disk and only then answers. Nothing else writes a board.

beats.heading: The browser is a viewer
beats.body: A pane holds board content only as a read-only cache of what the server said, and reads again when it is told a new version exists. What it owns is the camera, the view, the walkthrough position and what somebody picked out.

beats.heading: Pictures are taken outside the server
beats.body: rasterize paints the SVG the server drew in a headless browser the CLI starts. record opens the server's own page in one: the page plays the walkthrough, the Codex voice narrates it, and the CLI writes the tab's capture to a video file.

beats.heading: Agent work has a lifetime of its own
beats.body: The Archboard server owns a private Codex child in its own process group. Sign-in, config and threads live in one Codex home every Archboard server on this machine shares. A pane's thread link names one workhorse, voice belongs to its separate coordinator, and the child's exit invalidates the link rather than leaving it dangling. The threads author boards through the CLI, like any agent.

beats.heading: The skill is measured, not assumed
beats.body: The guidance an agent in another repository reads is held to real runs: two versions of the package, the same CLI and fixtures, real authors, and a blinded grading session. A person starts it; the gate never does.

beats.heading: Agent work has a lifetime of its own
beats.body: The Archboard server owns a private Codex child in its own process group. Sign-in, config and threads live in one Codex home that every Archboard server on this machine shares. A minute after a tab closes, its conversation ends, and Codex unloads its threads once no work runs on them. When the child exits, each tab starts a new conversation with its next message.
